ti: Fix reduceKernel — closure call, odometer and F32 pre-widening on every element
Make broadcastKernel copy contiguous runs instead of walking an odometer per element
Remove the per-element indirect call and bounds checks from the elementwise kernels

note: Implemented and validated. broadcastKernel hoists the innermost axis out of the per-element odometer: each run is a copy (source stride 1) or a fill (stride 0), and the odometer ticks once per run. MEASURED 160,540 -> 35,730 ns on BenchmarkBroadcastF64_256to256x256, 4.49x, via an interleaved three-round A/B with a file-copy toggle on the same host in one session. An earlier non-interleaved comparison suggested 5.5x and was DISCARDED: the untouched BenchmarkReshapeF64_64K control moved 46.4 to 37.0 us between those sessions, proving the runs were not comparable. BIT-IDENTITY: exact equality rather than tolerance, since the op does no arithmetic. TestBroadcastRunsMatchesPerElement pins it element-for-element against the per-element traversal across F32 and F64 for a trailing verbatim row, a trailing broadcast axis, a mixed rank-3 case and a rank-0 output; proven NON-VACUOUS by mutation (moving the odometer tick to the innermost axis turns it red, restoring turns it green). Added BenchmarkBroadcastReplicateF64 and BenchmarkBroadcastMixedF64 for the regimes the pre-existing benchmark never covered. Gates: gofmt and go vet clean, backend/... and autograd green; nn carries two pre-existing bit-identity failures identical on unmodified main (goai#385), unrelated. NOT DONE: the perfscan rule for the scalar-copy-with-contiguous-run pattern remains outstanding and is still required by the standing contract; left to the detector work rather than bundled here. Recorded in docs/benchmarking.md.

body:
SHIPPED. Both reflector applications in the reference QR — to the trailing columns of R and to the Q accumulator — ran one column at a time, accumulating down a strided column and then walking it again to update. With the column index innermost both passes stream contiguous rows and the reflector element is loop-invariant across the row. BenchmarkQR_128x64 -35.0 percent (1032564 to 671655 ns). Cost is one n-length scratch reused across all k: 297688 to 298200 B/op and one more allocation.

THE SECOND CELL IS THE VALUABLE MEASUREMENT. BenchmarkQR_32x16 did not move at all — at that size the whole factorization is L1-resident, so the layout it walks stops mattering. One kernel, one transform, worth a third at one size and nothing at another. That is what PS6011 means when it says its premise is a cache claim it cannot make, and the check now carries this pair so the caveat is actionable instead of abstract: a small benchmark cell will report a real transform as noise, and a large one will oversell it for a caller who never gets there.

BIT-IDENTICAL: every per-column dot still accumulates over ascending i with the same operands and every update still subtracts the same product; only the order in which INDEPENDENT columns are visited changes. TestQRInterchangeIsBitIdentical holds the pre-interchange factorization verbatim and compares BOTH outputs on raw bits across a square case, a tall one, and n=1 where the trailing loop is empty. Three mutations pin what it sees: swapping the operands of the scale and of the update both stay GREEN, correctly, since IEEE multiplication is commutative, while reversing the accumulation order reddens it — which is precisely the property the interchange had to preserve.

CORRECTION TO AN EARLIER RECORD: a previous round listed the ref QR column walks as blocked on a missing benchmark. They were not — BenchmarkQR_128x64 and QR_32x16 already existed. The autograd QR VJP is the one without instrumentation. Two different kernels with the same name got conflated.

STILL OPEN: ref SVD column walks (svdKernel, matTmulRect and the m>n correction), the autograd QR and SVD VJPs, gguf largest-first claiming (needs a skewed-size benchmark) and ReadRaw per-tensor copy.
